title: Benefit jobs and a Zulu grand marshal's funeral
summary: Williams tells of a good-hearted man at Sam's who died, a woman who collected three hundred dollars with a cigar box to hire the band, and a Zulu grand marshal buried with scrounged money.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well that was uh... They jumped me up on the floor at Sam.

He was riding in Ramport, that's where we used to pass him. A guy, he was a good, a good Samurit, he used to give a good play on the card game, the Pity Pat game at Sam's where they sell those uh, those Samurit's, poor boy Sam. So they thought they'd give him a big cent off because he was a good fellow, he just took sick and he died. Uh-huh. And I was hired by Boynese Briscoe.

She hired the band. Talking without a day. And I'm always wanting to bring that picture and let us see that picture. Uh-huh. She hired the band and uh, she walked for me around in Ramport with a cigar box to Beanz's, to Ramport and Grabier.
And uh, she picked up about three hundred dollars. So what I'd give him was Swingin' Time for the Week. Uh-huh. And Tom Hades been the band, watched for the Zulus all these days.
He died, he wasn't leading the band. He was one of the great grand marshal.
He died. They didn't have no money to bury him when he died.
They didn't have a band? Yeah, they had a band but they had to-
Cigar box. Yeah, they had to scalp like hell. Uh-huh. They never had no money to treasure.
